history.prompt: Core KYB for a financial institution opening a business bank account. Work the stages an onboarding file is built from, in this order: customer identification, whether a legally registered entity exists, is active, and is the applicant; beneficial ownership and control, including what can only come from the customer; the nature and purpose of the account, meaning whether the business is actually operating and what is expected to flow through it; sanctions, PEP and watchlist screening; and adverse information and financial standing. Then recommend whether to onboard, and name the steps that complete the case file.

result.headline: Onboard subject to conditions: identification and screening are complete, but the account should not open until the adverse media source and the recent lien are read and the ownership certification, standing certificate and operating checks are on the file.

body.text: Middesk sells business identity infrastructure to regulated financial institutions — banks, lenders and fintech platforms that have to verify a business customer before opening an account or extending credit. It pulls filings from state and federal registries behind an API, and sells verification, ongoing monitoring and agent-assisted state registration on top of that data. Revenue is subscription and per-verification fees from those institutions.

This stage is satisfied. Four independent handles agree on the same entity: the submitted name matches the state registrations, the submitted office address matches an address carried on a registration, the entity type reads as a corporation against the domestic filing, and the IRS holds a record for the submitted TIN and business name together. The TIN pairing is the strongest of the four, because it is the one handle an applicant cannot assert into existence — it either exists at the IRS against that name or it does not.

Registration standing is the part of the stage still open, and it is open because of what the states publish rather than because of anything on the record. Five filings sit here: two active — including the one in the state of the submitted office address — one inactive, and two returning no status at all. For a company that registers where it does business, a mixed picture across five states is the ordinary shape. The filing that cannot be read is the domestic one: the state of formation returns no status and publishes no good-standing sub-status through this channel, so the registration a reviewer would most want evidenced is the one no order will produce.

gaps.point: Whether the domestic registration is active and in good standing
gaps.wouldAnswer: The state publishes neither a status nor a good-standing sub-status through this channel, so no order returns one. A Certificate of Good Standing obtained by the customer is the only route.

body.text: The rule asks for two different kinds of person — the natural persons owning 25 percent or more, and at least one individual with significant control — and the record reaches only the second. A submitted person matches an officer named on the state registrations, which establishes a control person against a public filing rather than against the applicant's own word; that is the stronger of the two evidentiary routes and it is the one already closed. Ownership percentages are published nowhere the record can read, so they arrive as a customer certification or they do not arrive at all.

Twenty related businesses share officers, agents or addresses with this one. For a company registered in five states that is the footprint of founders and registered agents sitting across several entities rather than a finding in itself, but it is the list to read before a certification is accepted rather than after — an owner named on the certification who also appears across these entities is a different disclosure than one who does not.

gaps.point: The natural persons who own 25 percent or more of the entity, as distinct from the officer already matched
gaps.wouldAnswer: Officers are published and matched; ownership percentages are not published anywhere the catalog reaches. A signed beneficial-ownership certification naming each owner, with identifying details screened the way the submitted person was, is what closes it.

body.text: The physical side of this stage holds. The submitted office address is deliverable and commercial, which is what a real place of business looks like rather than a mailbox, and the wider address footprint reads as registered-agent offices rather than as concentration: three addresses are shared with twenty or fewer businesses, one with between twenty-one and a hundred, and five with more than a hundred — the expected signature of registering in five states, not of a shared-address operation.

The trading side is where the file is thinnest. No website, domain or third-party profile check returned on this pull, and no industry classification returned either. For a company whose product is delivered over the web to regulated institutions, those are the most direct evidence available that the business is operating as described, and none of it is here — which leaves operating status resting on the registrations alone and leaves expected activity resting on the application rather than on anything corroborated.

gaps.point: Whether the company's website and online presence corroborate the application
gaps.wouldAnswer: The catalog defines website, domain and third-party profile checks and none returned on this pull.

gaps.point: The line of work on record, and the volumes and counterparties expected through the account
gaps.wouldAnswer: No industry classification returned on this pull. Classification plus the customer's stated expected activity is what a nature-and-purpose record is built from.

body.text: This stage returns a finished answer, which is worth distinguishing from a stage that merely raises nothing: the checks ran and cleared. No watchlist hits against the business or the submitted individuals, and no politically exposed persons among those individuals or their relatives and close associates. Of the five stages in this file it is the only one complete as it stands, and it is the one that would have to be re-run against any beneficial owners the certification names.

Three findings on this record point at the business rather than at the limits of the data, and none of the three is characterised. Adverse media returned one or more high risk sources with no article behind it. A lien was filed within the past three months, with no amount and no secured party. Ten related litigations sit alongside them, with no subject matter and no indication whether the business is plaintiff or defendant.

What each of them has in common is that the record carries the existence of a thing without the thing itself, and that is the distance between them and a usable finding. For a company of this size ten litigations is an ordinary number and says little on its own; a lien filed inside three months and a high risk media score are recent and specific enough that the underlying documents change what they mean. Against all three, the record is clear on bankruptcy: there are no filings.

gaps.point: What the high risk adverse media source says, and whether it concerns this business
gaps.wouldAnswer: The record carries the score and not the source. The articles behind it are what decide whether this is a name collision or a finding.

gaps.point: What the new lien secures, its amount, and the secured party
gaps.wouldAnswer: A lien filed in the last three months is recent enough to bear on the decision, and the record carries its existence without its size.

gaps.point: Whether the ten litigations are ordinary commercial matters, and whether the business is plaintiff or defendant
gaps.wouldAnswer: Ten is a count, not a characterisation. Reading them is what separates routine contract disputes from anything connected to the adverse media.

body.text: Nothing on this record argues against the relationship — what is outstanding is the file, and it separates into four kinds of work. Two items are conditions precedent: the adverse media source and the lien in Adverse information have to be read before anyone can weigh them, and an unread high risk score is not something an approval can carry. Two are collections from the customer: the beneficial-ownership certification, which is the only route to the owners because nothing publishes them, and the good-standing certificate the state of formation will not publish. Two are orders that simply did not return on this pull — the website and profile checks, and industry classification. One is a policy decision the bank makes about itself rather than about this business: whether its accepted-industry list covers business-verification software sold to regulated institutions. Customer identification and screening are already complete, so none of the remaining work reopens them.

followUps.text: Pull the adverse media source and read it, since a high risk score with no article behind it can be neither cleared nor acted on and it is the item most likely to change the decision.
Obtain the lien filing — amount, secured party and what it secures — because one filed within the last three months bears on both the account decision and any later credit exposure.
Read the ten litigations for subject matter and for whether the business is plaintiff or defendant, and check whether any of them is the source behind the adverse media hit.

Collect a signed beneficial-ownership certification naming every natural person owning 25 percent or more, then screen each of them against watchlists and PEP lists the way the matched officer already was.
Request a Certificate of Good Standing for the state of formation from the customer, which is the only evidence of standing available because the state publishes none.
Order the website, domain and third-party profile checks so that operating status rests on more than registrations for a company whose product is delivered over the web.

Order industry classification and take the customer's stated expected activity — volumes, counterparties and payment types — then decide whether the line of work sits inside the accepted-industry policy.

Assemble the case file in stage order — identification evidence, the ownership certification, standing and operating documents, then the screening and adverse dispositions — and date-stamp each item so the next periodic review knows what was relied on and when.
Set the monitoring terms before the account funds: refresh liens, litigation and adverse media on a fixed cycle, and treat a change in registration status or a new officer as a trigger for re-review.
